set.tovw: Lead grade D (treasure thread): forum and web tellings only; a 1930 local called the saloon story a hoax

m-tr-rc-2.st: A TreasureNet telling adds the 'Hole in the Ground' saloon of Alph Berlanquette (or Bellanguette) on the beach about 2 miles from Fayette in the 1870s, used by the furnace workers; its owner is the one said to have buried his fortune.
m-tr-rc-2.t: A later Petoskey News item quotes a local, Rogers, that no one has hunted near Fayette recently despite reports that the owner of a nearby saloon buried his fortune: 'I think that story's a hoax.' The saloon site, about 2 miles from Fayette, is not placed.
src: TreasureNet thread 568960 (Hole in the Ground saloon)

tw-ia-north-mcgregor-taylor-gold.st: The 1905 wire as printed: in 1830 four bags of gold coin, $80,000 for the soldiers' pay, reached Col. Zachary Taylor's fort ('Fort McKay'). Fearing attack, he sent four trusted men to hide them; the fort was attacked, and after days of fighting the four were found dead. A scrap of paper near the body of the man called Mercierre said the money was 'buried on the highest of the bluffs across from the place where they were found'. Parties searched and found nothing; 'hundreds of people have worked by the day' on the lonely bluff near North McGregor, and in 1905 a premium was being offered.
tw-ia-north-mcgregor-taylor-gold.t: The 1905 telling is garbled history: Taylor commanded Fort Crawford at Prairie du Chien (1829-37), not 'Fort McKay' (the 1814 British name), the Black Hawk War was 1832, and no $80,000 pay shipment or massacre of a four-man detail is on record (the War Department told Laird in 1927 it had no record of any lost sum). Treat the amount and the 1830 date as legend; the 'highest bluff across from' the finding place is the only locating clue.
src: "Treasure Hidden," Rock Island Argus, 18 Mar 1905, p. 3 (Chronicling America sn92053934); same wire Evening Times-Republican (Marshalltown), 16 Mar 1905, p. 3 (earliest print found, sn85049554), and St. Paul Globe, 3 Apr 1905, p. 2; reprinted North Iowa Times, 20 Jul 1905
